# Agent Guide
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/agent/guide/

The Crontinel agent is a lightweight daemon that runs on your server, connects to `app.crontinel.com`, and polls for remote commands. It enables cloud-triggered cron execution — schedule a command from the dashboard and the agent runs it on your server.

:::caution[Command allowlist required]
By default the agent refuses to run **any** command. You must explicitly configure an allowlist of permitted commands before the agent will execute anything triggered from the dashboard — see [Command Allowlisting](#command-allowlisting) below. This is deliberate: the dashboard can schedule an arbitrary command, so the agent won't run it unless you've told it that command is expected.
:::

## How It Works

1. The agent registers with Crontinel Cloud using your API key and app ID
2. It connects to receive commands — see [Connection Method](#connection-method) below, since this differs by runtime
3. When a trigger is scheduled from the dashboard, the agent checks the command against your configured allowlist
4. If allowed, it executes the command and reports the result (success/failure, output, duration) back to the cloud; if not allowed, it reports a rejection and does **not** run it
5. A heartbeat is sent every 60 seconds to confirm the agent is alive

### Connection Method

The Laravel agent and the Node.js/Python agents use different transports to receive commands:

- **Laravel** opens a persistent SSE (Server-Sent Events) connection to `/v1/agent/stream` and receives commands as they're dispatched, with no polling interval. Heartbeats are sent separately via `/v1/agent/heartbeat` every 60 seconds.
- **Node.js and Python** poll `app.crontinel.com/api/v1/agents/{id}/commands` every 5 seconds, and send heartbeats via `/api/v1/agents/heartbeat` every 60 seconds.

Both approaches deliver the same behavior from your perspective — commands run within seconds of being scheduled — the underlying connection just differs by runtime.

## Laravel Agent

The Laravel package (`crontinel/laravel`) includes a built-in agent command.

### Prerequisites

- `crontinel/laravel` installed via Composer
- `CRONTINEL_API_KEY` and `CRONTINEL_APP_ID` set in `.env`

### Start the Agent

```bash
php artisan crontinel:agent
```

### Production Setup

Generate a systemd unit file:

```bash
php artisan crontinel:agent --systemd
```

Or a supervisor config:

```bash
php artisan crontinel:agent --supervisor
```

## Node.js Agent

The Node package (`@crontinel/node`) includes a CLI agent.

### Prerequisites

- `@crontinel/node` installed via npm
- `CRONTINEL_API_KEY` and `CRONTINEL_APP_ID` environment variables set

### Start the Agent

```bash
npx crontinel agent
```

Or with environment variables inline:

```bash
CRONTINEL_API_KEY=your-key CRONTINEL_APP_ID=your-app npx crontinel agent
```

## Python Agent

The Python package includes an agent CLI (requires PyPI installation when available).

### Prerequisites

- `crontinel` package installed
- `CRONTINEL_API_KEY` and `CRONTINEL_APP_ID` environment variables set

### Start the Agent

```bash
crontinel agent
```

## Check-in alerts

Set how often an agent should check in from **Configure** on its row in the dashboard: an expected interval and a grace period.

- **Missed:** when an agent misses its expected check-in, Crontinel sends an alert. When it checks in on time again, you get a recovery notice. A repeat of the same alert waits at least 15 minutes.
- **Late:** turn on **Alert when late** to also get a separate alert once a check-in is past its interval. It is off by default and recovers when the agent is on time.

To silence one agent for a while, use the mute control on its row. See [muting alerts](/alerts/channels/#muting-alerts-saas).

## Command Allowlisting

The agent will only execute commands that match an entry in your allowlist. An unconfigured or empty allowlist means **no commands are permitted** — this is the default, fail-closed behavior.

Patterns support exact string matches and `*` as a wildcard (e.g. `php artisan queue:*` allows any `queue:` subcommand).

**Laravel** — publish the config (`php artisan vendor:publish --tag=crontinel-config`) and set `allowed_commands` in the `agent` block of `config/crontinel.php`:

```php
'agent' => [
    // ...
    'allowed_commands' => [
        'php artisan queue:restart',
        'php artisan horizon:terminate',
        'php artisan queue:*',
    ],
],
```

**Node.js and Python** — set the `CRONTINEL_AGENT_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` environment variable to a comma-separated list of patterns:

```bash
CRONTINEL_AGENT_ALLOWED_COMMANDS="php artisan queue:restart,php artisan horizon:terminate,queue:*" npx crontinel agent
```

The Node.js and Python agents also accept an equivalent `allowedCommands` / `allowed_commands` option when constructing the agent programmatically.

A rejected command is reported back to the dashboard as failed with the reason "Command rejected: not in allowlist," so you can see rejections in your trigger history and adjust the allowlist as needed.

## Systemd Service (All Runtimes)

Create `/etc/systemd/system/crontinel-agent.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Crontinel Agent Daemon
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=www-data
WorkingDirectory=/path/to/your/app
Environment=CRONTINEL_API_KEY=your-api-key
Environment=CRONTINEL_APP_ID=your-app-slug
ExecStart=/usr/bin/php artisan crontinel:agent
Restart=always
RestartSec=10

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Enable and start:

```bash
sudo systemctl enable crontinel-agent
sudo systemctl start crontinel-agent
```

## Supervisor Config (All Runtimes)

Create `/etc/supervisor/conf.d/crontinel-agent.conf`:

```ini
[program:crontinel-agent]
command=php artisan crontinel:agent
directory=/path/to/your/app
user=www-data
autostart=true
autorestart=true
startretries=3
stderr_logfile=/var/log/crontinel-agent.err.log
stdout_logfile=/var/log/crontinel-agent.out.log
```

Reload and start:

```bash
sudo supervisorctl reread
sudo supervisorctl update
sudo supervisorctl start crontinel-agent
```

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CRONTINEL_API_KEY` | Yes | — | Your API key from app.crontinel.com/settings |
| `CRONTINEL_APP_ID` | Yes | — | Your app slug from the app settings page |
| `CRONTINEL_API_URL` | No | `https://app.crontinel.com` | API base URL (change only for self-hosted) |
| `CRONTINEL_AGENT_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` | Node/Python only | — (fail-closed) | Comma-separated allowlist patterns. Laravel uses `allowed_commands` in `config/crontinel.php` instead — see [Command Allowlisting](#command-allowlisting) |

## Testing

1. Add the command you want to test to your [allowlist](#command-allowlisting) — untested commands are rejected by default
2. Go to your app detail page
3. Click "Schedule Trigger"
4. Enter the same command (e.g., `php artisan inspire`)
5. Set it to run "Now"
6. Watch the agent execute it and report back

## Troubleshooting

**Agent won't start**
- Verify `CRONTINEL_API_KEY` and `CRONTINEL_APP_ID` are set
- Check network connectivity to `app.crontinel.com`

**Agent starts but no commands received**
- Verify the app ID matches your app in the dashboard
- Check that triggers are being dispatched (Dashboard → Triggers)

**Agent crashes repeatedly**
- Enable logging: set `CRONTINEL_AGENT_LOG=/var/log/crontinel-agent.log`
- Ensure the agent user has permission to execute the scheduled commands

**Commands are rejected / never execute**
- Check the trigger's result on the dashboard for "Command rejected: not in allowlist"
- Verify the command matches an entry in your [allowlist](#command-allowlisting) exactly, or via a `*` pattern
- Remember the default allowlist is empty — nothing runs until you configure one

# Alert Channels
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/alerts/channels/

Channels work the same for every runtime. Add them in the Crontinel dashboard: a curl, Node, Python, Sidekiq, or GitHub Actions job gets the same alert on a failed outcome, a run that never starts, or a run that never finishes. The environment variables further down configure the Laravel package's local alerting only.

## Available channels

| Channel | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Slack | `webhook_url` | Incoming webhook URL |
| Email | `to` | Recipient email address |
| Webhook | `url` | Any HTTPS endpoint |
| PagerDuty | — | Coming soon |
| SMS | — | Coming soon |
| OpsGenie | — | Future roadmap |
| VictorOps | — | Future roadmap |

## Configuration

### Slack

**OSS: configure via environment variables**

In your `.env`:
```env
CRONTINEL_ALERT_CHANNEL=slack  # Required environment variable
CRONTINEL_SLACK_WEBHOOK=https://hooks.slack.com/services/YOUR/WEBHOOK/URL  # Required environment variable
```

Or directly in `config/crontinel.php` under the `alerts` key.

Set up an [Incoming Webhook](https://api.slack.com/messaging/webhooks) in your Slack app, then add the channel in the Crontinel dashboard with config key `webhook_url`.

### Email

**OSS: configure via environment variables**

In your `.env`:
```env
CRONTINEL_ALERT_CHANNEL=email  # Required environment variable
CRONTINEL_ALERT_EMAIL=you@example.com  # Required environment variable
```

Add an email channel with config key `to` set to the recipient address. Crontinel sends via Resend  –  no SMTP setup required on your end.

### PagerDuty (coming soon)

> **Note:** PagerDuty integration is planned and will be available in a future release.

### Webhook

**OSS: configure via environment variables**

In your `.env`:
```env
CRONTINEL_ALERT_CHANNEL=webhook  # Required environment variable
CRONTINEL_WEBHOOK_URL=https://your-endpoint.example.com/crontinel  # Required environment variable
```

Add a webhook channel with config key `url`. Crontinel sends a POST with:

```json
{
  "app": "my-app",
  "alert_key": "queue:default:depth",
  "message": "Queue 'default' depth is 1500 (threshold: 1000)",
  "state": "firing",
  "fired_at": "2026-04-07T08:00:00Z"
}
```

## Alert deduplication

The same condition won't re-fire for 5 minutes. If a queue stays above its threshold for an hour, you get one alert at the start  –  not one every poll cycle.

## Auto-resolution

When a condition clears, Crontinel sends a "resolved" notification. You get clear start and end signals for every incident.

## Muting alerts (SaaS)

Mute alerts for 1 hour, 4 hours, 24 hours, or 7 days, or unmute early. Only people who can configure the app can mute.

- **Whole app:** use the mute control in the app header.
- **One monitor:** use the mute control on a cron, heartbeat, HTTP, cron schedule, or agent row. A muted cron schedule also mutes run alerts for its command.

While muted, Crontinel still records incidents and state. Only the notification is held back. An app mute wins over monitor settings. Test sends still go out. The mute ends by itself, and each mute and unmute is in the audit log.

## Maintenance windows (SaaS)

Plan quiet time ahead instead of muting by hand. Add windows on the app's **Settings** tab, under **Maintenance windows**. You need configure access to the app.

- **Once:** a start and end date and time.
- **Weekly:** the days, a start time and a duration (5 minutes to 7 days). Times use the app's time zone, or UTC if it has none, and follow daylight saving changes. A Sunday 09:00 window stays at 09:00 local time all year.
- **Scope:** the whole app, or only the monitors you pick, or only monitors with the tags you list. With no monitors and no tags, the window covers the whole app. A cron schedule in scope also covers run alerts for its command.

During a window:

- Alerts in scope send no notifications and no escalation steps. Escalation steps are not used up.
- Incidents are still recorded. Open alerts show **During maintenance**.
- A cron schedule occurrence due inside the window does not raise a "never started" alert, even after the window ends.
- The app header shows **In maintenance until** the window's end, with **(selected monitors)** when the window has a scope.

When a window ends, an incident in scope that is still open and unacknowledged gets one normal notification, and escalation starts its wait again from that point. An incident that recovered during the window sends nothing.

Each add, edit and delete is in the audit log. You can also manage windows with the [Configuration API](/reference/config-api/#maintenance-windows). Status page maintenance windows are separate and do not affect alerts.

## Acknowledging alerts (SaaS)

Acknowledge an open alert to say someone is on it. It stops escalation for that incident only.

- **Dashboard:** the app's Monitors tab lists open alerts. Click **Acknowledge**. You need configure access to the app.
- **Email and Slack:** firing alerts include an **Acknowledge this alert** link. It works without signing in, covers that one incident, and expires after 24 hours. The link opens a confirm page; nothing changes until you press **Acknowledge**.

Each open alert shows who acknowledged it and when. Every acknowledgement is in the audit log, with the user or the channel link as the actor. The recovery notification still goes to every channel that was notified. If the alert fires again after it recovered, that is a new incident and starts unacknowledged.

## Escalation (SaaS)

Set an escalation policy per app on the app's **Settings** tab, under **Escalation**. A policy has up to 5 steps. Each step waits 5 to 1440 minutes after the previous step, then notifies the channels you pick.

- The first notification goes out as it always does. Channels you pick in a step are held back until that step, so a PagerDuty or SMS channel can wait for step 1.
- Escalation stops when someone acknowledges the alert or the alert recovers.
- Only alerts that open after you first add a policy escalate. Alerts already open at that time do not. Editing the policy later does not change this.
- Each step sends once per incident. Escalation messages start with `Escalation step N, not acknowledged:`.
- A muted app or a [maintenance window](#maintenance-windows-saas) holds escalation back. The step is not used up; it sends once the mute or window ends if the alert is still open and unacknowledged.
- Recovery notifies every channel the incident reached, including escalation channels.

Open alerts show **Escalated to step N** once a step has gone out. You can also read and replace the policy with the [Configuration API](/reference/config-api/#escalation-policy).

## SaaS alert management

In the [Crontinel SaaS](https://app.crontinel.com) you can configure per-app alert channels through the web UI without touching config files.

## Future alert channels

The following channels are on the roadmap but not yet available:

- **PagerDuty** — IT alert routing and incident management. Planned for a future release.
- **SMS** — Direct text message alerts. Sign up for early access at [crontinel.com](https://crontinel.com/) when this launches.
- **OpsGenie** — IT alert routing and on-call management. Planned for a future release.
- **VictorOps** — Incident management and PagerDuty alternative. Planned for a future release.

# CLI Health Check
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/alerts/cli/

```bash
php artisan crontinel:check
```

Prints a table of all monitor statuses and exits:
- `0`  –  all monitors healthy
- `1`  –  one or more alerts active

## JSON output

```bash
php artisan crontinel:check --format=json
```

Returns:

```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "horizon": {"status": "running", "paused": false},
  "queues": [{"name": "default", "depth": 5, "status": "ok"}],
  "crons": [{"command": "inspire", "last_exit_code": 0, "status": "ok"}],
  "alerts": []
}
```

## CI/CD usage

```yaml
# GitHub Actions
- name: Check job health
  run: php artisan crontinel:check --format=json
```

```bash
# Deploy script
php artisan crontinel:check || echo "Warning: monitors unhealthy after deploy"
```

## No-alert mode

Run the check without firing alerts (useful for health endpoints):

```bash
php artisan crontinel:check --no-alerts
```

## What the check covers

The command reads the same three monitors as the dashboard: Horizon (running or paused), each watched queue (depth against its threshold), and the latest run of each scheduled command (exit code). The `alerts` array in the JSON output lists whatever is currently firing, so a pipeline can print it when the exit code is `1`.

`crontinel:check` ships with the [Laravel package](/sdks/laravel/) and needs `php artisan`. If your job runs in another runtime, use an [HTTP check-in](/check-in/recipes/) and [register the schedule](/check-in/schedule/) instead; the hosted app does the alerting.

## Related

- [Alert channels](/alerts/channels/) for where fired alerts are sent
- [Cron monitor](/monitors/cron/), [queue monitor](/monitors/queues/), and [Horizon monitor](/monitors/horizon/) for the thresholds behind each status
- [Configuration reference](/reference/configuration/) for every threshold key
- [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting/) if the command exits `1` and you do not know why

# Analytics and Run History
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/analytics/

Each app has an **Analytics** page, linked from the app navigation. It shows how every job has done over a time range. It works for any runtime that sends [receipts](/check-in/recipes/).

## Ranges

Pick **24h**, **7d**, **30d**, or **90d**. Ranges longer than your plan's history retention are not shown.

Days follow the app's timezone setting. If the app has no timezone set, days are UTC.

## What it shows

Summary tiles at the top: runs, success rate, failures, outcome unknown, and incidents.

Then one row per job:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Runs | Runs in the range |
| Success | Share of finished runs that succeeded. Runs with an unknown outcome are left out of both the count and the total. |
| Failed | Runs that failed |
| Outcome failed | Runs that exited 0 but failed an [outcome rule](/check-in/start-finish/#outcome-rules-and-missing-evidence) |
| Outcome unknown | Runs that exited 0 but did not send the evidence an outcome rule needs. Not a success and not a failure. |
| Late | Runs marked late |
| Missed | Runs that never started when expected |
| p50, p95 | Median and 95th percentile duration |
| Quality pass | Share of AI-graded runs that met the pass score. Blank unless the job has a [quality check](/mcp/ai-agent-monitoring/#quality-check-ai-optional). |

A **Daily trend** chart shows success rate and p95 duration per day for each job. If the app reports queues, a **Queues (daily max)** table shows the highest depth and oldest job age per queue per day.

Missed and incident counts come from incident history. Full history starts on 2026-10-31. Before that date, only the latest incident for each alert is counted.

## Run history

**All runs** opens the run history: 50 runs per page, newest first. Filter by range, job, and status (`completed`, `failed`, `late`, `running`, `outcome failed`, or `outcome unknown`). `completed` lists only runs whose outcome is passed or has no rule. The **Quality (AI)** column shows the grade when the job has a quality check.

The dashboard's history tab also links here with **View all runs**.

## CSV export

**Export CSV** downloads the runs that match the current range and filters. Anyone who can view the app can export. An export holds up to 50,000 rows.

Columns: `id`, `command`, `status`, `outcome_status`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `attempt`, `trigger_source`.

## Weekly email

Turn on **Email me a weekly report for each app in my organizations** on your profile. It is off by default.

The email goes out on Mondays at 08:00 UTC. For each app it covers the last 7 full days in the app's timezone and shows runs, success rate, incidents, and the slowest jobs by p95. Turn it off from the same profile setting.

## Related

- [Alert channels](/alerts/channels/): where alerts go, and how to mute them
- [AI agent jobs](/mcp/ai-agent-monitoring/): guardrails and quality checks
- [Billing and plans](/billing/): plan allowances

# Billing & Plans
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/billing/

Paid plans are **Starter**, **Pro**, and **Max**. Free remains the $0 plan. The old Free/Pro/Team capacity table is retired. The Laravel package is MIT and free to use locally without an account.

Owner-selected prices (matching Stripe test-mode prices; not a production checkout acceptance claim):

| Plan | Monthly | Annual | Internal key |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Free | $0 | — | `free` |
| Starter | $9.99 | $99.90 | `starter` |
| Pro | $19.99 | $199.90 | `pro` |
| Max | $49.99 | $499.90 | `team` |

Annual totals are about two months free against monthly billing. Prefer monthly until annual billing is verified. There is no forever-price promise and no contractual response SLA.

## Monthly allowances

Approved organization allowances (enforcement and hosted cost acceptance are separate gates):

| Plan | Accepted ingest requests | Submitted JSON body bytes | Hosted AI starts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Free | 20,000 | 64 MiB | 5 |
| Starter | 100,000 | 256 MiB | 20 |
| Pro | 500,000 | 1 GiB | 50 |
| Max | 2,000,000 | 4 GiB | 100 |

AI quality grades have their own monthly allowance: Free 50, Starter 500, Pro 2,000, Max 5,000. Each graded run uses one, even when the grade fails. See [AI agent jobs](/mcp/ai-agent-monitoring/#grade-allowance).

Allowances reset at 00:00 UTC on the first day of the month. Bytes are submitted request body size, not retained storage. There is no overage charge. A rejected ingest returns a typed 429. Ordinary MCP reads from your own assistant do not spend hosted AI starts.

## Included on every tier

- OAuth-default MCP and generated scoped API keys
- Outcome rules (numeric minimum and artifact freshness). Missing evidence is not healthy.
- Deterministic **email** alerts for failure and recovery, including an incorrect business result, whether or not a model is available

## Not on the sold card yet

- Slack, customer webhooks, SMS, or on-call as a paid channel until each passes the same delivery test as email
- Monitor / app / member caps or retention days copied from the retired Free/Pro/Team proposal
- Customer status pages, uptime probes, or badges as part of this offer

See the [pricing page](https://crontinel.com/pricing/) on the marketing site for what is published today. Workspace contract: `PRICING.md` in the Crontinel workspace.

## Upgrading and cancelling

Manage billing from the [Billing page](https://app.crontinel.com/team/billing) in the dashboard. Cancel anytime; the subscription stays active until the end of the current period, then Free allowances apply.

## OSS

`crontinel/laravel` is MIT licensed. Self-hosted local dashboards are not a substitute for hosted detection when the same host dies. See [Self-Hosting](/self-hosting/).

# Deploy markers
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/check-in/deploy-markers/

Send one request from your deploy pipeline and Crontinel records a deploy marker. When a job starts failing, you can see whether a release went out just before it.

Markers show up in four places:

- **Analytics.** A purple vertical line on each day of the daily trend that had a deploy.
- **Run history.** A deploy row between the runs before and after it.
- **Open alerts.** "Last deploy before this: `v2.4.0 (production)` (40 minutes earlier)" under each open alert.
- **Incident evidence.** AI investigations and the MCP `get_incident_evidence` tool get up to 3 deploys from the 24 hours before the incident. They get the version, environment, commit SHA, and time, never the description or URL. A deploy near an incident is timing only. It does not prove the deploy caused it.

## Send a deploy

Use the app **ingest key** (`CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY`), the same key as [run receipts](/check-in/recipes/).

```bash
curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 -X POST "https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/deploy" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"version":"v2.4.0","environment":"production","commit_sha":"9fceb02d0ae598e95dc970b74767f19372d61af8"}'
```

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | yes | Release name, tag, or build number. Up to 100 characters. |
| `environment` | no | For example `production` or `staging`. Up to 100 characters. |
| `commit_sha` | no | Hex, 4 to 64 characters. |
| `deployed_at` | no | ISO 8601. Defaults to now. Must not be more than five minutes in the future. |
| `url` | no | `https://` only, for example the CI run or release page. |
| `description` | no | Up to 500 characters. Shown in run history. |

The first request for a version returns `201` with `"created": true`. Sending the same version for the same environment again returns `200` with `"created": false` and the same `deploy_id`. The stored marker stays as it was, so retries are safe. The same version in two environments makes two markers.

Each request counts against the monthly ingest allowance like any other receipt. When it runs out you get the same [typed `429`](/reference/api/#ingest-endpoints) with `Retry-After`.

## GitHub Actions

Add a step after your deploy step. Store `CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY` as a repository secret. `|| true` keeps a monitoring hiccup from failing the deploy.

```yaml
- name: Record deploy in Crontinel
  if: success()
  env:
    CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY: ${{ secrets.CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY }}
  run: |
    curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 -X POST "https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/deploy" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d "{\"version\":\"${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ github.run_number }}\",\"environment\":\"production\",\"commit_sha\":\"${{ github.sha }}\",\"url\":\"${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}\"}" \
      || true
```

Re-running the workflow reuses `github.run_number`, so a re-run lands on the same marker.

## Read deploys back

- REST: `GET /api/v1/apps/{slug}/deploys` returns the 50 most recent markers, newest first. Add `?environment=production` to filter. See the [REST API](/reference/api/#get-appsslugdeploys).
- MCP: `list_deploys` (needs `run:read`) lists markers for an app. Values come from your pipeline, so assistants treat them as untrusted data.

---

# Ping URLs (no API key)
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/check-in/ping-urls/

Each cron schedule in Crontinel has a ping URL. The token in the URL is the credential, so the job needs no API key and no JSON. Find the URL on the app's **Cron schedules** page, next to each schedule. Only members who can configure the app see it.

A ping goes through the same path as a [JSON receipt](/check-in/recipes/). Schedule checks, outcome rules, AI quality checks, alerts, and the monthly ingest allowance all work the same way.

## Endpoints

`GET` and `POST` both work.

| URL | Records |
|---|---|
| `https://app.crontinel.com/ping/<token>` | A completed run |
| `https://app.crontinel.com/ping/<token>/start` | A running run |
| `https://app.crontinel.com/ping/<token>/fail` | A failed run |
| `https://app.crontinel.com/ping/<token>/<exit_code>` | Completed for `0`, failed for anything else. The exit code is stored. |

A successful ping returns `200` with the body `OK`.

## Examples

```bash
# Finished
curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 https://app.crontinel.com/ping/<token>

# Failed
curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 https://app.crontinel.com/ping/<token>/fail

# Report the job's exit code
./backup.sh
curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 https://app.crontinel.com/ping/<token>/$?

# Send the job's output (first 10,000 characters are kept)
./backup.sh > /tmp/backup.log 2>&1
curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 --data-binary @/tmp/backup.log https://app.crontinel.com/ping/<token>/$?
```

In a crontab line:

```bash
0 2 * * * /opt/jobs/backup.sh && curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 https://app.crontinel.com/ping/<token>
```

## Start and finish

Ping `/start` when the job begins to get an alert for a run that starts and never finishes within the schedule's maximum runtime.

```bash
RID="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 "https://app.crontinel.com/ping/<token>/start?rid=$RID"
./backup.sh
curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 "https://app.crontinel.com/ping/<token>/$??rid=$RID"
```

- `rid` (run id) pairs the start with the finish. Use 1 to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_` or `:`. Pass it in the query string.
- Without `rid`, a finish closes the latest open run that this URL started. That works when runs of the job never overlap.
- Repeating a finish for a run that already finished returns `OK` and changes nothing, so `--retry` is safe.
- The run's duration is the time between the start and finish pings.

## Errors

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `404` | Unknown or regenerated token. The body is `Not found`, with no other details. |
| `422` | Invalid `rid` |
| `429` | Too many pings: 60 per minute per URL. Or the organization used its monthly ingest allowance; that response is the same JSON as the [ingest API](/reference/api/). |

## Regenerate the URL

If a URL leaks, click **Regenerate ping URL** on the schedule. The old URL stops working at once and returns `404`. The change is recorded in the audit log.

## Outcome rules with pings

A ping carries no `outcomes` metrics. If an outcome rule applies to the job, its runs will show the outcome as [unknown](/check-in/start-finish/#outcome-rules-and-missing-evidence). Use a [JSON receipt](/check-in/recipes/) when the job needs to report numbers such as `processed_records`.

---

# Check-in from any runtime
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/check-in/recipes/

Crontinel is an outcome monitor for background work in whatever runtime already runs it. Every runtime posts the same JSON receipt. Exit code 0 can still fail an outcome rule when `processed_records` is 0 and the rule requires work. If the number is missing, the outcome is [unknown](/check-in/start-finish/#outcome-rules-and-missing-evidence), never healthy.

**First-class runtimes on this page:** system cron (curl), Node.js, Python, Sidekiq/Ruby, and GitHub Actions. Laravel is the maintained deep package for schedule attach, queue depth, and Horizon — not a requirement for outcome monitoring.

Use the **app ingest key** (`CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY`). It is not an MCP key. A monitoring failure must not fail the business job.

The examples under **Universal receipt** show the receipt itself. To catch a job that crashes, wrap the job so it sends `failed` with its exit code instead of nothing: see the runtime sections below. A job that crashes before it sends a receipt is otherwise invisible unless you also [register its schedule](/check-in/schedule/).

## Universal receipt

### curl

```bash
export CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY=your-app-ingest-key
curl -sS -X POST "https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/cron" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"request_key":"run-1","command":"reports:generate","status":"completed","exit_code":0,"started_at":"2026-10-06T12:00:00Z","finished_at":"2026-10-06T12:00:05Z","outcomes":{"metrics":{"processed_records":0}}}'
```

### Python

Download `outcome_checkin.py` once. It uses only the Python standard library (3.8+). There is no supported PyPI package for this path.

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://docs.crontinel.com/outcome_checkin.py
```

No `curl`, as on slim container images? Fetch it with Python. Send a `User-Agent`: the docs site refuses Python's default one.

```bash
python3 -c "import urllib.request as u; r = u.Request('https://docs.crontinel.com/outcome_checkin.py', headers={'User-Agent': 'crontinel-checkin'}); open('outcome_checkin.py', 'wb').write(u.urlopen(r).read())"
```

```bash
python3 outcome_checkin.py \
  --command reports:generate \
  --request-key run-1 \
  --exit-code 0 \
  --started-at 2026-10-06T12:00:00Z \
  --finished-at 2026-10-06T12:00:05Z \
  --records 0 \
  --url https://app.crontinel.com \
  --api-key "$CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY"
```

### Node

```js
await fetch("https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/cron", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    request_key: "run-1",
    command: "reports:generate",
    status: "completed",
    exit_code: 0,
    started_at: "2026-10-06T12:00:00Z",
    finished_at: "2026-10-06T12:00:05Z",
    outcomes: { metrics: { processed_records: 0 } },
  }),
});
```

## Node scheduler (node-cron, BullMQ)

Wrap the scheduled function. This is an HTTP example, not an npm package.

```js


async function postReceipt({ requestKey, command, exitCode, startedAt, records }) {
  const body = {
    request_key: requestKey,
    command,
    status: exitCode === 0 ? "completed" : "failed",
    exit_code: exitCode,
    started_at: startedAt,
    finished_at: new Date().toISOString(),
    outcomes: { metrics: { processed_records: records } },
  };
  try {
    await fetch("https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/cron", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY}`,
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify(body),
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000),
    });
  } catch {
    // Monitoring must not fail the business job.
  }
}

cron.schedule("0 3 * * *", async () => {
  const startedAt = new Date().toISOString();
  let exitCode = 0;
  let records = 0;
  try {
    records = await generateReports();
  } catch (error) {
    exitCode = 1;
    throw error;
  } finally {
    await postReceipt({ requestKey: `node-reports-${startedAt}`, command: "reports:generate", exitCode, startedAt, records });
  }
});
```

For BullMQ, call `postReceipt` from the worker's `completed` and `failed` handlers and use the job id as `request_key`.

## Python schedulers (APScheduler, Celery)

Both wrap the task the same way. `build_receipt` comes from `outcome_checkin.py` (see the Python section above).

```python

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from outcome_checkin import build_receipt

def now():
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")

def post_receipt(request_key, exit_code, started, records):
    body = build_receipt(
        command="reports:generate",
        request_key=request_key,
        exit_code=exit_code,
        started_at=started,
        finished_at=now(),
        processed_records=records,
    )
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/cron",
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={
            "Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY"],
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
        method="POST",
    )
    try:
        urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5)
    except Exception:
        pass  # Monitoring must not fail the business job.

# APScheduler
@sched.scheduled_job("cron", hour=3)
def reports_generate():
    started, exit_code, records = now(), 0, 0
    try:
        records = run_reports()
    except Exception:
        exit_code = 1
        raise
    finally:
        post_receipt(f"apscheduler-{started}", exit_code, started, records)

# Celery (schedule with Beat as you already do)
@shared_task(bind=True)
def reports_generate(self):
    started, exit_code, records = now(), 0, 0
    try:
        records = run_reports()
        return records
    except Exception:
        exit_code = 1
        raise
    finally:
        post_receipt(f"celery-{self.request.id}-{started}", exit_code, started, records)
```

Crontinel does not discover Celery Beat or APScheduler entries. Name the jobs you expect with [a registered schedule](/check-in/schedule/).

## System cron

Wrap the job, capture exit code and times, post the receipt, and keep monitoring from failing the job (`|| true`).

```bash
STARTED_AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
set +e
/usr/local/bin/generate-reports
EXIT_CODE=$?
set -e
FINISHED_AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
python3 outcome_checkin.py \
  --command reports:generate \
  --request-key "reports-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)" \
  --exit-code "$EXIT_CODE" \
  --started-at "$STARTED_AT" \
  --finished-at "$FINISHED_AT" \
  --records "${RECORDS:-0}" \
  --url https://app.crontinel.com \
  --api-key "$CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY" \
  || true
exit "$EXIT_CODE"
```

## GitHub Actions

Store `CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY` as a repository secret. Put this step last. GitHub skips later steps after a failed step unless they say `if: always()`, so without it a failed workflow sends nothing. `job.status` decides whether the receipt says `completed` or `failed`. Replace the `0` with your count. The `request_key` uses `run_id`, `run_attempt` and the job name, so a re-run and a sibling job in the same workflow each record their own run. A matrix repeats the job name, so add `${{ matrix.<key> }}` to the key there. `|| true` keeps a Crontinel outage from failing the workflow.

```yaml
- name: Report outcome
  if: always() # also runs when an earlier step failed
  env:
    CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY: ${{ secrets.CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY }}
    JOB_STATUS: ${{ job.status }}
  run: |
    status=completed; code=0; outcomes=',"outcomes":{"metrics":{"processed_records":0}}' # replace 0 with your count
    if [ "$JOB_STATUS" != success ]; then status=failed; code=1; outcomes=''; fi
    curl -sS -m 10 -X POST "https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/cron" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d "{\"request_key\":\"gha-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-${{ github.job }}\",\"command\":\"reports:generate\",\"status\":\"$status\",\"exit_code\":$code,\"started_at\":\"$(date -u +%FT%TZ)\"$outcomes}" \
      || true
```

## Sidekiq / Ruby

Wrap the job. A completed run sends the count; a job that raises sends `failed` and re-raises, so Sidekiq still retries as usual. The receipt method rescues, so a Crontinel problem never fails or mislabels the job. There is no supported gem for this path.

```ruby
require "net/http"
require "json"
require "time"

class ReportsGenerateJob
  include Sidekiq::Job

  def perform
    started = Time.now.utc.iso8601
    records = Reports.generate! # return how many records it processed
    crontinel_receipt(started, "completed", 0, records)
  rescue StandardError
    crontinel_receipt(started, "failed", 1, nil)
    raise # Sidekiq still sees the failure and retries as usual
  end

  private

  def crontinel_receipt(started, status, exit_code, records)
    uri = URI("https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/cron")
    req = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri)
    req["Authorization"] = "Bearer #{ENV.fetch("CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY")}"
    req["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    body = { request_key: "sidekiq-#{jid}-#{started}", command: "reports:generate", status: status,
             exit_code: exit_code, started_at: started, finished_at: Time.now.utc.iso8601 }
    body[:outcomes] = { metrics: { processed_records: records } } unless records.nil?
    req.body = body.to_json
    Net::HTTP.start(uri.hostname, uri.port, use_ssl: true) { |http| http.request(req) }
  rescue StandardError
    # Monitoring must never fail the job.
  end
end
```

A failed run carries no count, so it raises the failed alert and not also an outcome alert.

Nothing changes when `sidekiq-cron` or `sidekiq-scheduler` enqueues the job: the receipt lives in `perform`, so scheduled and manual runs report the same way. Crontinel does not read their schedules. Register the job with [a schedule](/check-in/schedule/) and a stopped Sidekiq process alerts as a run that never started. Sidekiq's default retries send one `failed` receipt per attempt, so a crashing job shows several failed runs and one alert.

## Scheduled agents

Reuse the same rules: report items produced as `processed_records` (or artifact time as `latest_artifact`). An empty successful agent run is a failed outcome when the rule requires work. This is not a separate AI-agent product.

## Laravel (deep integration)

When you need schedule attach, queue depth, and Horizon freshness, install the Composer package:

```bash
composer require crontinel/laravel
php artisan crontinel:install
```

See [Laravel](/sdks/laravel/) and [Installation](/installation/). Do not tell a non-Laravel operator to install Composer.

## Verify

1. Send `processed_records: 0` with exit code 0.
2. Confirm the outcome alert (business result failed).
3. Send a later run with a passing count and confirm recovery.

Coverage stays unknown until you name the job. Crontinel does not read crontab or an agent runner.

## Not claimed here

- Language SDK parity for Node, Python, Go, Rust, Ruby, or .NET
- Crontab or Kubernetes auto-discovery
- LLM spend or tracing products

---

# Register expected jobs over HTTP
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/check-in/schedule/

A receipt tells Crontinel a job ran. Registering the job tells Crontinel it **should** run. With both, you get an alert when a run never starts, even if nothing was posted.

No Laravel package is needed. Use the same **app ingest key** as the [check-in recipes](/check-in/recipes/).

## Register a job

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/schedule" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "source": "named_by_user",
    "tasks": [{
      "command": "nightly-import",
      "job_name": "nightly-import",
      "expression": "0 2 * * *",
      "timezone": "UTC",
      "grace_seconds": 300,
      "max_runtime_seconds": 3600,
      "counted_minimum": 1
    }]
  }'
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | yes | `named_by_user` for HTTP runtimes. |
| `tasks[].command` | yes | The exact `command` your receipts send. Runs are matched on it. |
| `tasks[].job_name` | no | Stable name that survives a command change. If you set it, send the same `job_name` on every run receipt, or the job's rules won't apply to those runs. |
| `tasks[].expression` | no | Five-field cron expression. Without it the job is inventory only and no missed-run check runs. |
| `tasks[].timezone` | no | IANA time zone for the expression. Default `UTC`. |
| `tasks[].grace_seconds` | no | How late a start may be before it alerts. Default `300`, or `900` for a command starting with `agent:`. |
| `tasks[].max_runtime_seconds` | no | How long a `running` receipt may stay open before it alerts as unfinished. Default `3600`, or `7200` for a command starting with `agent:`. |
| `tasks[].counted_minimum` | no | Creates a `processed_records` rule: fewer than this fails the run even on exit 0. |

If you register a `job_name`, add it to every receipt for that job, for example `"job_name": "nightly-import"` next to `"command"`. Rules for a named job follow the name, so a receipt without it is treated as a different, unnamed job. Leave `job_name` out of both to match on `command` alone.

Scheduled AI agents get longer defaults because model calls vary. Name the job with an `agent:` prefix, such as `agent:nightly-digest`, and leave the two timing fields out. Values you send always win. See [AI agent jobs](/mcp/ai-agent-monitoring/) for token, cost, and tool-call ceilings and the optional quality check.

The response lists `created`, `unchanged`, `activated` (an existing named job that gained its schedule), and `skipped` (plan limit). Posting the same body again is safe.

## Node and Python

```js
await fetch("https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/schedule", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    source: "named_by_user",
    tasks: [{ command: "nightly-import", expression: "0 2 * * *", counted_minimum: 1 }],
  }),
});
```

```python


req = urllib.request.Request(
    "https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/schedule",
    data=json.dumps({
        "source": "named_by_user",
        "tasks": [{"command": "nightly-import", "expression": "0 2 * * *", "counted_minimum": 1}],
    }).encode(),
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY']}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
)
urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5)
```

## What happens next

- Checking starts when you register. Earlier occurrences are not checked.
- If no receipt with that `command` starts between the due time and the grace period, a **cron never started** alert opens. It resolves once the next scheduled run is observed.
- If a `running` receipt is still open after `max_runtime_seconds`, a **cron never finished** alert opens. See [start and finish receipts](/check-in/start-finish/).
- If a run completes but took longer than `max_runtime_seconds`, a **cron ran too long** alert opens. The next run inside the limit resolves it.
- `check_monitoring_coverage` over MCP names the registered jobs instead of reporting the inventory as unknown. It does not read crontab or an agent runner.

Laravel apps don't need this request: `php artisan crontinel:schedule` (package v0.9.2 or later) registers the Laravel schedule the same way, with timezones. Earlier versions stored it as inventory only.

---

# Start and finish receipts
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/check-in/start-finish/

One receipt after the job finishes is enough for outcome rules. Add a `running` receipt at the start when you also want an alert for a job that starts and never ends.

## The pair

Use the same `request_key` for both. The key identifies one execution.

```bash
KEY="nightly-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
STARTED="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
post() {
  curl -sS -m 5 -X POST "https://app.crontinel.com/api/v1/ingest/cron" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$1" || true
}

post "{\"request_key\":\"$KEY\",\"command\":\"nightly-import\",\"status\":\"running\",\"started_at\":\"$STARTED\"}"

./nightly-import.sh
CODE=$?
RECORDS=$(cat /tmp/nightly-import.count 2>/dev/null || echo 0)

STATUS=completed; [ "$CODE" -ne 0 ] && STATUS=failed
post "{\"request_key\":\"$KEY\",\"command\":\"nightly-import\",\"status\":\"$STATUS\",\"exit_code\":$CODE,\"started_at\":\"$STARTED\",\"finished_at\":\"$(date -u +%FT%TZ)\",\"outcomes\":{\"metrics\":{\"processed_records\":$RECORDS}}}"
exit $CODE
```

Rules for the pair:

- `started_at` must be the same in both receipts. A different identity under the same key returns 409.
- A finished run (`completed` or `failed`) cannot be changed or reopened. Use a new key for a retry.
- A late `running` receipt after the finish is ignored.
- `|| true` and `-m 5` keep a monitoring failure from failing the business job.

## What each receipt unlocks

| You send | Alert you get |
|---|---|
| Only the finish receipt | Outcome failures (exit code, `processed_records`) and unknown outcomes when the metric is missing. |
| Finish receipt plus a [registered schedule](/check-in/schedule/) | Also: the run never started. |
| `running` plus a registered schedule | Also: the run started and never finished within `max_runtime_seconds`. |

Fields are listed in the [ingest reference](/reference/api/#post-ingestcron). For jobs that can only run curl, the [ping URL](/check-in/ping-urls/) of a schedule does the same without an API key.

## Outcome rules and missing evidence

An outcome rule checks a metric or timestamp from the finish receipt, for example `processed_records` at least 1. Each completed run gets one of three outcome results:

| Outcome | When |
|---|---|
| `passed` | Every rule had its evidence and met it. |
| `failed` | At least one rule had its evidence and did not meet it. |
| `unknown` | No rule failed, but at least one rule's metric or timestamp was not in the receipt. |

Unknown is not success. It is never shown in green, on the dashboard, in run history, in analytics, or over MCP.

### Missing-value policy

Each rule has a setting for missing evidence, under **When the evidence is missing** on the **Outcome rules** page:

- **Unknown** (default). The run's outcome is unknown. Crontinel opens an **outcome unknown** alert with the text "No evidence received for `<metric>`". It is separate from the outcome-failed alert. It recovers on the next run whose receipt includes the evidence. An unknown run does not close an open outcome-failed alert.
- **Fail the rule.** Missing evidence fails the rule, as a value below the minimum would. Use it when a missing number means the job is broken.

Rules created before this setting existed use **Unknown**.

---

# FAQ
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/faq/

## Do I need Laravel?

No. Every runtime posts the same HTTP outcome receipt. First-class paths: curl, Node, Python, Sidekiq, and GitHub Actions. See [check-in recipes](/check-in/recipes/) and [quick start](/quick-start/).

Laravel is optional. Use `crontinel/laravel` when you want the package to attach that receipt from the scheduler and add queue depth or Horizon freshness.

## Do I need a crontinel.com account?

For hosted alerts and the dashboard, yes — create an app and use the ingest key (`CRONTINEL_INGEST_KEY`). That key is not an MCP / assistant key.

The Laravel package can also run a local `/crontinel` dashboard without a hosted account. That local path is not a substitute for hosted detection when the same host dies.

## How do I send my first receipt?

1. Create an app at [app.crontinel.com](https://app.crontinel.com/login).
2. Copy the ingest key.
3. POST to `/api/v1/ingest/cron` when the job finishes (curl, Node `fetch`, `outcome_checkin.py`, Sidekiq, or GitHub Actions).
4. Send `processed_records: 0`, confirm the outcome alert, then send a later count and confirm recovery.

Recipes: [check-in recipes](/check-in/recipes/).

## Will Crontinel slow down my application?

For HTTP check-in, you control when the POST runs (usually after the job). Keep a short timeout and do not fail the business job if monitoring fails.

On Laravel with the package, monitoring listens to scheduler events. When `CRONTINEL_API_KEY` is set, the package reports over HTTP with a short timeout; a monitoring failure does not fail your task. Omit the key for local-only dashboard use.

## Does the Laravel package work with Octane?

Yes. It uses standard service provider and event patterns. Keep queue workers separate from the Octane server, as Laravel recommends generally.

## What happens if app.crontinel.com goes down?

Your jobs keep running. Receipts that cannot be delivered should not fail the business work (recipes use `|| true` / rescue where shown). On Laravel with only a local dashboard, that dashboard stays independent of the hosted app.

## What data is sent to the hosted app?

Nothing until you use an ingest key. A receipt can include command / job name, status, exit code, times, and optional outcome metrics or timestamps you set. Queue and Horizon snapshots are Laravel-package paths only.

**No application payloads, user PII, or environment secrets should be put in the receipt.**

## What are the plan names and prices?

Paid plans are **Starter**, **Pro**, and **Max** (internal Max key remains `team`). Free remains $0. See [Billing & Plans](/billing/) for allowances. The marketing price card stays gated until billing acceptance; [crontinel.com/pricing](https://crontinel.com/pricing/) shows what is published today.

## How do I upgrade the Laravel package?

```bash
composer require crontinel/laravel:^0.9
php artisan migrate
php artisan crontinel:check
```

See the [changelog](https://github.com/crontinel/laravel/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) and [upgrading](/upgrading/).

## Where is the comparison or Slack on the price card?

Comparison publish and sold Slack/webhook channels wait on operator interviews and delivery verification (customer tasks S7–S10). Email outcome alerts are the verified channel today.

---

# Installation
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/installation/

## Not on Laravel?

Post one HTTP receipt when the job finishes. First-class paths: curl, Node, Python, Sidekiq, and GitHub Actions. See the [HTTP check-in recipes](/check-in/recipes/) and [quick start](/quick-start/). You do not need Composer.

## Laravel package

The rest of this page is for Laravel apps that want the package to attach that receipt from the scheduler and add queue depth and Horizon freshness.

### 1. Prerequisites

- PHP 8.2+
- Laravel 11, 12, or 13
- A Crontinel account ([sign up free](https://app.crontinel.com/login))

### 2. Install

```bash
composer require crontinel/laravel
php artisan crontinel:install
php artisan migrate
```

### 3. Configure

By default the dashboard is at `/crontinel`. Optionally change it in your `.env`:

```env
CRONTINEL_PATH=crontinel
```

### 4. Open the dashboard

Visit `/crontinel` while signed in to your app. You'll see the monitoring dashboard.

The dashboard needs a signed-in user, so your app needs a `login` route. `crontinel:install` warns you if it doesn't have one. Any signed-in user can open the dashboard until you limit it, so if your customers can sign in to this app, [define the `crontinel.view` gate](/reference/configuration/#middleware).

> **What you should see:** The Horizon and Queue sections populate immediately. The Cron section will be empty until your scheduler has run at least once — this is normal.

### 5. Run your scheduler

For local development:

```bash
php artisan schedule:work
```

For production, add this to your server's crontab:

```bash
* * * * * cd /path-to-your-project && php artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1
```

### 6. Dashboard verification

After the first scheduler tick:

1. Go to `/crontinel` in your browser
2. The **Cron** section now shows your registered scheduled commands
3. Each command displays its last run time, duration, and status

<Aside>
The Laravel package works fully offline with no external API key required. To send data to the Crontinel SaaS, add `CRONTINEL_API_KEY` to your `.env`.
</Aside>

---

## Laravel package details

Still not on Laravel? Stop here and use the [HTTP recipes](/check-in/recipes/). Everything below is Composer-only.

### Requirements

- PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, or 8.5
- Laravel 11, 12, or 13

### Install (repeat of the quickstart)

```bash
composer require crontinel/laravel
php artisan crontinel:install
php artisan migrate
```

After running the installer, `config/crontinel.php` is published to your project. Review it to set the dashboard path, middleware, and alert thresholds. See the [configuration reference](/reference/configuration/) for all available options.

> **Using Horizon?** Set `'horizon' => ['enabled' => true]` in `config/crontinel.php`. If you're not using Horizon, set it to `false` to hide the Horizon panel.

## Dashboard path

By default the dashboard is at `/crontinel`. To change it:

```env
CRONTINEL_PATH=monitoring  # Required environment variable
```

## Middleware

The dashboard uses `['web', 'auth']` middleware by default. To customize:

```php
// config/crontinel.php
'middleware' => ['web', 'auth', 'can:view-monitoring'],
```

## Requirements check

```bash
php artisan crontinel:check
```

Exits 0 if healthy, 1 if any alert is active. Use in CI pipelines:

```bash
php artisan crontinel:check --format=json
```

## Environment variables

All Crontinel environment variables and their defaults. Set these in `.env` or directly in `config/crontinel.php`:

```env
# Dashboard path (default: /crontinel)
CRONTINEL_PATH=crontinel

# Horizon integration (set to false if you don't use Horizon)
CRONTINEL_HORIZON=true
CRONTINEL_HORIZON_CONNECTION=horizon

# Alert channel (slack, email, webhook)
CRONTINEL_ALERT_CHANNEL=slack
CRONTINEL_SLACK_WEBHOOK=https://hooks.slack.com/services/YOUR/WEBHOOK/URL
CRONTINEL_ALERT_EMAIL=alerts@example.com
CRONTINEL_WEBHOOK_URL=https://your-endpoint.example.com/crontinel
# PagerDuty is on the alerts roadmap — see /alerts/channels

# SaaS reporting (optional — omit for local-only monitoring)
CRONTINEL_API_KEY=
CRONTINEL_API_URL=https://app.crontinel.com
```

See the [configuration reference](/reference/configuration/) for all options including thresholds, retention, and middleware.

## Upgrading

Pull the latest version through Composer:

```bash
composer update crontinel/laravel
```

If you want to pin a specific version, use `composer require crontinel/laravel:^0.9` instead.

### Run new migrations

New releases sometimes add or modify tables. After updating, always run:

```bash
php artisan migrate
```

The package uses its own migration files, so this is safe to run alongside your app migrations. Check the release notes if you're curious what changed.

### Config changes

If a new version introduces config options, your existing `config/crontinel.php` won't have them. You've got two choices:

1. Re-publish and diff manually:

```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=crontinel-config
```

This will ask to overwrite your existing file. Say no, then compare the new defaults with your current config.

2. Check the changelog for new keys and add them yourself. This is usually faster if only one or two options were added.

### Check for breaking changes

Before upgrading across major versions, read the [changelog](https://github.com/crontinel/laravel/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). Major releases may rename config keys, drop support for older Laravel/PHP versions, or change method signatures. In practice, minor and patch releases won't break anything.

### Verify the upgrade

Once you've migrated and updated your config, run the health check:

```bash
php artisan crontinel:check
```

This reads Horizon, your queues and your scheduled commands, then exits `1` if any of them is in an alert state. It doesn't test your API key or the connection to Crontinel.

So, the full upgrade sequence looks like this:

```bash
composer update crontinel/laravel
php artisan migrate
php artisan crontinel:check
```

Three commands, done in under a minute.

---

# Introduction
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/introduction/

**Completed is not done.** A process can exit 0 and still produce nothing. Crontinel keeps process status and business result as separate states. Missing evidence is never shown as healthy.

## The problem

Generic monitors check whether a heartbeat arrived or a URL returned 200. They cannot tell you:

- That a nightly import exited 0 with `processed_records: 0`
- That a scheduled agent wrote an empty digest
- That Horizon or a queue stopped reporting freshness (Laravel package path)

## How it works

1. Your job posts an HTTP receipt to `/api/v1/ingest/cron` with the command, exit code, times, and optional outcome metrics.
2. Crontinel evaluates schedule and outcome rules on the server.
3. Alerts fire without waiting for a model. Your coding assistant can read the same evidence over MCP.

First-class check-in paths: curl, Node, Python, Sidekiq, and GitHub Actions — see [HTTP recipes](/check-in/recipes/). The [Laravel package](/sdks/laravel/) is the deep integration: it attaches that receipt from the scheduler and can add queue depth and Horizon freshness. Unowned language packages are not a support claim.

## Plans and pricing

See the [pricing page](https://crontinel.com/pricing/) on the marketing site for current tiers. Hosted monitoring and alerts do not depend on a language SDK.

## Open source

The Laravel package is MIT licensed. Self-hosted local dashboards are not a substitute for hosted detection when the same host dies.

## Where to go next

- [Quick start](/quick-start/): send your first receipt in a few minutes
- [Check-in recipes](/check-in/recipes/): curl, Node, Python, Sidekiq, and GitHub Actions
- [Register expected jobs](/check-in/schedule/): get an alert when a run never starts
- [Start and finish receipts](/check-in/start-finish/): get an alert when a run never finishes
- [Laravel installation](/installation/): schedule, queue, and Horizon evidence
- [MCP overview](/mcp/overview/): read the same evidence from Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex
- [Billing and plans](/billing/) and [security](/security/)
- [FAQ](/faq/) and [troubleshooting](/troubleshooting/)

---

# AI Agent Jobs
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/mcp/ai-agent-monitoring/

A scheduled AI agent is a job. It posts the same [receipt](/check-in/recipes/) as any other runtime. Crontinel then checks three things: the run happened, it produced what you expect, and it stayed inside the limits you set.

## Name and register the job

Name the job with an `agent:` prefix, such as `agent:nightly-digest`, and [register it](/check-in/schedule/). Agent jobs get longer default grace and runtime limits because model calls vary.

## Report guardrail numbers

Your agent reports its own numbers under `outcomes.metrics` on the finish receipt:

```json
{
  "command": "agent:nightly-digest",
  "status": "completed",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "output": "...",
  "outcomes": {
    "metrics": {
      "items_produced": 12,
      "tokens_used": 48210,
      "cost_usd": 0.31,
      "tool_calls": 17
    }
  }
}
```

Then add one outcome rule per number. The **Outcome rules** page in the app has presets for each:

| Preset | Rule | Default threshold |
|---|---|---:|
| At least 1 item produced | `items_produced` numeric minimum | 1 |
| Token ceiling | `tokens_used` numeric maximum | 200000 |
| Cost ceiling | `cost_usd` numeric maximum | 5 |
| Tool-call ceiling (loop detection) | `tool_calls` numeric maximum | 50 |

A run over a ceiling fails its outcome rule, even on exit code 0. Change the thresholds to fit your agent. These rules check numbers your agent reports. Crontinel does not meter model usage.

## Quality check (AI, optional)

A quality check asks a model to grade a run's `output` against your rubric. It is off until you add one for a job.

To add one, open **Outcome rules** and fill in **Quality check (AI, optional)**:

- **Job name**, or the command when the job has no name
- **Rubric**: plain language, up to 1,000 characters
- **Pass score**: 1 to 5
- **Consent**: the run's output and your rubric are sent to Crontinel's hosted model provider (Cloudflare Workers AI) for every graded run. Do not turn this on for output that contains secrets or personal data.

Hosted AI must also be on for the organization. An owner turns it on from **Assistance**. An app can have up to 10 quality checks.

### How grading works

- Only completed runs with non-empty `output` are graded. The first 6,000 characters are sent.
- The model returns a score from 1 to 5. A score at or above the pass score is a pass.
- A score below the pass score opens a separate quality alert. A later passing run clears only that alert.
- The grade is advisory. It never changes the run's status and never resolves other alerts. Alerts for failed, late, or missed runs do not wait for it.
- A reply that is not a valid grade shows as **unknown**.
- When the monthly grade allowance is used up or the model is unavailable, the grade shows as **unavailable** and no alert fires.

### Grade allowance

Grades have their own monthly allowance, separate from hosted AI investigation starts:

| Plan | Quality grades per month |
|---|---:|
| Free | 50 |
| Starter | 500 |
| Pro | 2,000 |
| Max | 5,000 |

The allowance resets at 00:00 UTC on the 1st. A grade that fails still counts. Usage shows on the [Billing page](https://app.crontinel.com/team/billing).

### Where the grade shows

- The **Quality (AI)** column in [run history](/analytics/#run-history)
- The **Quality pass** rate in [Analytics](/analytics/)
- The MCP `list_runs` tool, as `quality` with `status`, `score`, `pass_score`, and `advisory: true`. The model's reasons and the output are not returned.
- Incident evidence, as the quality status and score

## Related

- [Register expected jobs](/check-in/schedule/): catch an agent run that never starts
- [Start and finish receipts](/check-in/start-finish/): catch an agent run that never finishes
- [Ingest reference](/reference/api/#post-ingestcron): every receipt field
- [Billing and plans](/billing/): monthly allowances

# Claude Code Setup
URL: https://docs.crontinel.com/mcp/claude-code/

:::note
The Crontinel SaaS is now in early access. [Create a free account](https://app.crontinel.com/login) to get started.
:::

## 1. Get your API key

Log in to [app.crontinel.com](https://app.crontinel.com), go to your app, and copy the API key.

## 2. Add to Claude Code config

Edit `~/.claude/settings.json` (or use the Claude Code settings UI):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "crontinel": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@crontinel/mcp-server"],
      "env": {
        "CRONTINEL_API_KEY": "your-api-key-here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## 3. Restart Claude Code

The Crontinel tools will appear in Claude Code's tool list.

## 4. Try it

Ask Claude Code:

- "Did my cron jobs run last night?"
- "What's the queue depth right now?"
- "Is Horizon healthy?"
- "Show me recent alerts"

## Troubleshooting

If tools don't appear, check that Node.js 18+ is installed:

```bash
node --version
```

If the API key is wrong you'll see `401 Unauthorized` in the MCP server output.

## What Claude Code can read

Once connected, Claude Code calls the tools listed on [Available Tools](/mcp/tools/): scheduled jobs and their last runs, queue depth, Horizon state, and recent alerts. Ordinary reads from your own assistant do not spend hosted AI starts (see [billing and plans](/billing/) for the allowances).

For new setups, prefer OAuth from the app's connection screen over a pasted key; the API key above is the fallback. The [MCP overview](/mcp/overview/) explains how the stdio server proxies to `app.crontinel.com/api/mcp`.

## Related

- [MCP overview](/mcp/overview/)
- [Agent guide](/agent/guide/) if you want cloud-triggered commands on your own server
- [Security](/security/) for how keys and scopes should be handled
- [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting/) for connection and 401 errors
